questions.content:
An Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream is receiving customer data that
contains personally identifiable information. A developer needs to remove
pattern-based customer identifiers from the data and store the modified data in
an Amazon S3 bucket.
What should the developer do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Implement Kinesis Data Firehose data transformation as an AWS Lambda function. Configure the function to remove the customer identifiers. Set an Amazon S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery stream.
answers.explanation: Kinesis Data Firehose supports data transformation using AWS Lambda functions, allowing pattern-based customer identifiers to be removed before data delivery. Configuring the Lambda function in the Firehose stream ensures the data is transformed inline and delivered securely to the specified S3 bucket. Using AWS managed services like Lambda and Firehose aligns with best practices for scalability, security, and ease of management.

answers.content: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Set the EC2 instance as the destination of the delivery stream. Run an application on the EC2 instance to remove the customer identifiers. Store the transformed data in an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Using an EC2 instance for transformation adds operational overhead and is less secure and scalable compared to managed Lambda transformations.

answers.content: Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service instance. Set the OpenSearch Service instance as the destination of the delivery stream. Use search and replace to remove the customer identifiers. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: OpenSearch Service is not designed for inline data transformation in Firehose streams and adds unnecessary complexity for simple data masking.

answers.content: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow to remove the customer identifiers. As the last step in the workflow, store the transformed data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set the workflow as the destination of the delivery stream.
answers.explanation: Step Functions are not natively supported as a Firehose destination, so this is not a viable method for real-time transformation and delivery.

questions.content:
An application uses Lambda functions to extract metadata from files uploaded to
an S3 bucket; the metadata is stored in Amazon DynamoDB. The application starts
behaving unexpectedly, and the developer wants to examine the logs of the Lambda
function code for errors.
Based on this system configuration, where would the developer find the logs?

answers.content: Amazon S3
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is a storage service, not used for Lambda function logs.

answers.content: AWS CloudTrail
answers.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls but does not capture Lambda code execution logs directly.

answers.content: Amazon CloudWatch
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda function logs are sent to Amazon CloudWatch by default for monitoring and troubleshooting. Amazon CloudWatch Logs Live Tail allows real-time streaming and filtering of Lambda logs, helping developers quickly identify errors. Neither Amazon S3, AWS CloudTrail, nor Amazon DynamoDB store Lambda function code execution logs. Using CloudWatch aligns with AWS best practices for centralized and managed logging of Lambda functions.

answers.content: Amazon DynamoDB
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a database service and does not store Lambda logs.

A developer is incorporating AWS X-Ray into an application that handles personal
identifiable information (PII). The application is hosted on Amazon EC2
instances. The application trace messages include encrypted PII and go to Amazon
CloudWatch. The developer needs to ensure that no PII goes outside of the EC2
instances.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Manually instrument the X-Ray SDK in the application code.
answers.explanation: Manually instrumenting the X-Ray SDK in the application code allows full control over what data is sent in traces, enabling the developer to ensure no PII leaves the EC2 instance. Using manual instrumentation supports encrypting PII and controlling data before it is sent to CloudWatch, aligning with the requirement that no PII goes outside the EC2 instances. The key facts indicate that the X-Ray SDK on EC2 applications decides on tracing and controls sampling, which supports managing sensitive data in the application layer.

answers.content: Use the X-Ray auto-instrumentation agent.
answers.explanation: The X-Ray auto-instrumentation agent cannot guarantee PII is excluded as it automatically captures data without granular control.

answers.content: Use Amazon Macie to detect and hide PII. Call the X-Ray API from AWS Lambda.
answers.explanation: Amazon Macie is for detecting PII but does not prevent PII from being sent outside EC2; also, calling the X-Ray API from Lambda does not meet the requirement of no PII leaving EC2 instances.

answers.content: Use AWS Distro for Open Telemetry.
answers.explanation: AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry is a custom instrumentation solution but does not inherently guarantee exclusion of PII from outgoing data without manual intervention.

questions.content:
A company needs to harden its container images before the images are in a
running state. The company's application uses Amazon Elastic Container Registry
(Amazon ECR) as an image registry. Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon
EKS) for compute, and an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that orchestrates a
continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflow.
Dynamic application security testing occurs in the final stage of the pipeline
after a new image is deployed to a development namespace in the EKS cluster. A
developer needs to place an analysis stage before this deployment to analyze the
container image earlier in the CI/CD pipeline.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational
efficiency?

answers.content: Build the container image and run the docker scan command locally. Mitigate any findings before pushing changes to the source code repository. Write a pre-commit hook that enforces the use of this workflow before commit.
answers.explanation: Local docker scan and pre-commit hooks require manual setup and enforcement which reduces operational efficiency and consistency across developers.

answers.content: Create a new CodePipeline stage that occurs after the container image is built. Configure ECR basic image scanning to scan on image push. Use an AWS Lambda function as the action provider. Configure the Lambda function to check the scan results and to fail the pipeline if there are findings.
answers.explanation: Amazon ECR basic image scanning on image push automatically scans container images for vulnerabilities immediately after the image is built and pushed to the registry. Integrating the scan in a CodePipeline stage after the container image is built ensures early detection of vulnerabilities before deployment, which aligns with the requirement to analyze images earlier in the CI/CD pipeline. Using a Lambda function to check scan results and fail the pipeline on findings provides automated gating to prevent insecure images from proceeding, increasing security and operational efficiency. This approach leverages managed AWS services (ECR image scanning, CodePipeline, Lambda) rather than manual or local scanning, meeting both security and operational efficiency priorities.

answers.content: Create a new CodePipeline stage that occurs after source code has been retrieved from its repository. Run a security scanner on the latest revision of the source code. Fail the pipeline if there are findings.
answers.explanation: Scanning source code for vulnerabilities does not harden the container image and does not meet the requirement to analyze the container image earlier in the pipeline.

answers.content: Add an action to the deployment stage of the pipeline so that the action occurs before the deployment to the EKS cluster. Configure ECR basic image scanning to scan on image push. Use an AWS Lambda function as the action provider. Configure the Lambda function to check the scan results and to fail the pipeline if there are findings.
answers.explanation: Placing the scan action immediately before deployment delays vulnerability detection, missing the requirement to analyze images earlier in the pipeline.

questions.content:
A developer is testing a new file storage application that uses an Amazon
CloudFront distribution to serve content from an Amazon S3 bucket. The
distribution accesses the S3 bucket by using an origin access identity (OAI).
The S3 bucket's permissions explicitly deny access to all other users.
The application prompts users to authenticate on a login page and then uses
signed cookies to allow users to access their personal storage directories. The
developer has configured the distribution to use its default cache behavior with
restricted viewer access and has set the origin to point to the S3 bucket.
However, when the developer tries to navigate to the login page, the developer
receives a 403 Forbidden error.
The developer needs to implement a solution to allow unauthenticated access to
the login page. The solution also must keep all private content secure.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Add a second cache behavior to the distribution with the same origin as the default cache behavior. Set the path pattern for the second cache behavior to the path of the login page, and make viewer access unrestricted. Keep the default cache behavior's settings unchanged.
answers.explanation: Creating a second cache behavior with the path pattern for the login page and making viewer access unrestricted allows unauthenticated users to access the login page without changing the security of the default cache behavior, which restricts access to private content. This approach adheres to AWS best practices by keeping the private content secure while allowing necessary public access. Using multiple cache behaviors with different viewer access settings is a standard managed service solution to handle varied access requirements within a single CloudFront distribution.

answers.content: Add a second cache behavior to the distribution with the same origin as the default cache behavior. Set the path pattern for the second cache behavior to *, and make viewer access restricted. Change the default cache behavior's path pattern to the path of the login page, and make viewer access unrestricted.
answers.explanation: Making viewer access unrestricted for the default cache behavior compromises security for all content, not just the login page.

answers.content: Add a second origin as a failover origin to the default cache behavior. Point the failover origin to the S3 bucket. Set the path pattern for the primary origin to *, and make viewer access restricted. Set the path pattern for the failover origin to the path of the login page, and make viewer access unrestricted.
answers.explanation: Failover origins are meant for availability, not for access control purposes, and setting an origin with unrestricted access conflicts with the requirement to keep private content secure.

answers.content: Add a bucket policy to the S3 bucket to allow read access. Set the resource on the policy to the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the login page object in the S3 bucket. Add a CloudFront function to the default cache behavior to redirect unauthorized requests to the login page's S3 URL.
answers.explanation: Adding a bucket policy to allow read access to the login page object exposes that object publicly via S3 directly, bypassing CloudFront security controls and is less secure.

developer wants to add end-to-end testing to the application to eliminate as

answers.explanation: Unit tests are part of development but deploying them with 'amplify push' does not ensure they run automatically in deployment.

answers.explanation: Adding a test phase to the amplify.yml build settings integrates testing into the CI/CD pipeline, ensuring tests run automatically with each build and deployment. Amplify applies settings in amplify.yml to all branches, making it the appropriate place to implement end-to-end testing. This approach aligns with AWS best practices of automating testing during the build process to catch bugs before reaching production.

questions.content:
A company has deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The company has
configured the Auto Scaling group that is associated with the Elastic Beanstalk
environment to have five Amazon EC2 instances. If the capacity is fewer than
four EC2 instances during the deployment, application performance degrades. The
company is using the all-at-once deployment policy.
What is the MOST cost-effective way to solve the deployment issue?

answers.content: Change the Auto Scaling group to six desired instances.
answers.explanation: Increasing desired instances to six increases cost permanently and is not cost-effective.

answers.content: Change the deployment policy to traffic splitting. Specify an evaluation time of 1 hour.
answers.explanation: Traffic splitting evaluation time of 1 hour may delay deployment and increase complexity and cost without addressing the capacity issue during deployment.

answers.content: Change the deployment policy to rolling with additional batch. Specify a batch size of 1.
answers.explanation: A rolling deployment with an additional batch allows additional instances to be added temporarily during deployment, maintaining capacity above the unhealthy threshold. Specifying a batch size of 1 ensures that only a minimal number of instances are updated at a time, maintaining performance. This is more cost-effective than increasing the desired capacity permanently. The all-at-once deployment can cause capacity to drop below 4, degrading performance.

answers.content: Change the deployment policy to rolling. Specify a batch size of 2.
answers.explanation: Rolling deployment with batch size 2 updates more instances simultaneously, risking capacity dropping below 4 during deployment.

answers.explanation: The question asks for a way to create test events for Lambda functions that can be created once and shared for editing by all members of an IAM developer group. Option B suggests configuring the event sharing settings to make the test events shareable. Other options require managing data outside Lambda (S3 or DynamoDB) or restrict sharing, which is less integrated and not ideal according to AWS best practices.

answers.content: Create and store the test events in Amazon DynamoDB. Allow access to DynamoDB by using IAM roles.

An engineer created an A/B test of a new feature on an Amazon CloudWatch
Evidently project. The engineer configured two variations of the feature
(Variation A and Variation B) for the test. The engineer wants to work
exclusively with Variation A. The engineer needs to make updates so that
Variation A is the only variation that appears when the engineer hits the
application's endpoint.

Which solution will meet this requirement?

answers.content: Add an override to the feature. Set the identifier of the override to the engineer's user ID. Set the variation to Variation A.
answers.explanation: An override in CloudWatch Evidently allows targeting a specific user or identifier with a specific variation of a feature. Setting the identifier of the override to the engineer's user ID and the variation to Variation A ensures that only Variation A appears for that user. This approach directly modifies the feature variation for a specific user without changing the experiment setup. Adding or modifying experiments is not the recommended way to force a single variation for exclusive use by one user.

answers.content: Add an override to the feature. Set the identifier of the override to Variation A. Set the variation to 100%.
answers.explanation: Incorrect use of override identifier; the identifier should be a user or entity ID, not the variation name, and '100%' is not a valid variation setting.

answers.content: Add an experiment to the project. Set the identifier of the experiment to Variation B. Set the variation to 0%.
answers.explanation: Experiment modification is not necessary or recommended for targeting a single variation for an individual user.

answers.content: Add an experiment to the project. Set the identifier of the experiment to the AWS account's account ISet the variation to Variation A.
answers.explanation: Similarly, adding an experiment with the AWS account ID and setting variation is not how to target a specific user to see only Variation A.
